title: Israeli Strike Kills Two Hamas Engineers in Gaza City's Tel al-Hawa Neighborhood; 13 Wounded
detail: An Israeli strike hit a car in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City on Sunday, September 13, 2026, killing at least two people and wounding 13 others. The IDF said the strike targeted two Hamas engineers, identified as Hassan Ali Abu Nada and Abd al-Rahim Ahmad Khalil Khawa, whom it accused of being involved in the development and production of weapons, advancing attacks on troops and civilians, and working to rebuild Hamas's military capabilities in violation of the October 2025 ceasefire; the military said it took steps to minimize harm to civilians. Palestinian health officials said the blast severely dismembered the two bodies, complicating identification, and appealed to the public for help. Civil defense teams inspected the burned-out wreckage while ambulances took the wounded to Al-Shifa Hospital. The strike followed a run of Israeli operations that officials said killed more than 20 Hamas operatives, including brigade and company commanders, over the preceding two weeks.

media.caption: Palestinians inspect the wreckage of a vehicle struck by an Israeli strike in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City, September 13, 2026

confidenceReason: The strike, death toll and wounded count are corroborated by both Israeli and Palestinian-facing Tier 2 outlets, but the identification of the two dead as Hamas 'engineers' rests solely on the IDF's own account -- Palestinian health officials said the bodies were too dismembered to independently identify at time of writing.

title: Israeli Settlers Storm Deir Jarir Village East of Ramallah, Open Fire Toward Homes, Block Village Entrance
detail: A group of Israeli settlers stormed the village of Deir Jarir, east of Ramallah in the central West Bank, on Sunday evening, September 13, 2026, opening live fire toward Palestinian homes in what residents described as an attempt to intimidate them; local youths responded, leading to skirmishes. WAFA reported no injuries. The settlers also closed the village's iron entrance gate, obstructing residents' movement in and out. The incident was one of several settler-violence reports across the West Bank that weekend; no arrests were reported.

confidenceReason: Reported by a single Tier 2 Palestinian outlet (WAFA); no Israeli military or independent international confirmation of the incident was available at time of writing.
